subject: ent
title: Salivary gland disorders

steps.tx: Salivary glands (parotid serous, submandibular mixed, sublingual and minor glands) fail by obstruction, infection, autoimmunity and tumours. **Sialolithiasis** stones favour submandibular gland (80 percent pattern: alkaline mucinous saliva, uphill duct course) causing mealtime swelling and pain (salivary colic) easing between meals, with stone palpable in floor of mouth or seen on imaging; hydration, massage, sialagogues, duct dilation or sialendoscopy and gland excision escalate.
steps.say: Meal swells jaw, stone in submandibular duct. Parotid tumours and floor mouth stones live apart.

steps.tx: **Acute parotitis** divides bacterial (dehydrated elderly, post operative, Staphylococcus aureus, pus from Stensen duct, unilateral) from viral mumps (bilateral parotid swelling, orchitis, pancreatitis, meningitis associations, vaccine preventable). Chronic sialadenitis scar ducts after stones or radiation. **Sjogren syndrome** autoimmune lymphocytic destruction dries eyes and mouth (sicca, Schirmer test, anti Ro La, lip biopsy focus score), swelling parotids, risking lymphoma transformation needing vigilance for persistent hard enlargement.
steps.say: Dry eyes, dry mouth, swollen parotids: Sjogren. Hard persistent parotid in Sjogren hunts lymphoma.

steps.tx: Salivary **tumours**: parotid hosts most tumours and most are benign; smaller gland, higher malignancy share (sublingual and minor worst). **Pleomorphic adenoma** is commonest parotid tumour: slow painless preauricular mass, mixed epithelial myoepithelial histology, treated by superficial parotidectomy with facial nerve preservation (enucleation alone recurs from pseudopods), small long term malignant transformation risk in neglected masses. Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is commonest malignant salivary tumour overall; adenoid cystic creeps perineurally with pain and late lung metastases over decades.
steps.say: Big gland, benign odds; small gland, malignant odds. Pleomorphic adenoma comes out with cuff, never shelled.

steps.tx: Facial nerve and Frey syndrome frame parotid surgery: nerve trunk at stylomastoid foramen branches pes anserinus through gland (tumour deep or superficial to nerve defines operation), weakness after surgery usually temporary neuropraxia when preserved. **Frey syndrome** (gustatory sweating and flushing) follows auriculotemporal miswiring of parasympathetics to sweat glands, tested Minor starch iodine. Warthin tumour (older male smokers, bilateral parotid tail, cystic) is second benign pattern. Persistent parotid mass in adult needs imaging and fine needle sampling, never open incisional biopsy (seeding and nerve risk).
steps.say: Parotid surgery dances on facial nerve. Sweating while eating after parotidectomy is Frey rewiring.
